scan.summary: This is Evergreen Botanicals' state license from the OLCC. It lets the company grow recreational marijuana at 2210 Bailey Hill Road, in an indoor Tier II grow with up to 10,000 sq ft of mature plant canopy, from March 3, 2026 through March 2, 2027. It is the agency's own document, so there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is renewing it on time, meeting its five conditions, and keeping it posted where the public can see it. All details are from page 1, the only page.
scan.freshness_note: This is the current one-year term, issued March 3, 2026, so it is about 7 months old. You do not need a newer copy until the Commission acts on the 2027 renewal. When that happens, replace this copy on file and on the wall.

conditions.evidence_expected: A current lease or deed for 2210 Bailey Hill Road, plus OLCC approval of any premises change before it happens

conditions.title: Track every marijuana item in the Cannabis Tracking System (CTS)

conditions.title: Every employee who handles marijuana items must hold a current OLCC marijuana worker permit

conditions.title: Keep video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 running, and keep recordings for at least 90 days
conditions.evidence_expected: A camera coverage map or security plan, a record showing how long recordings are kept (at least 90 days), and system maintenance or outage logs

conditions.title: Tell OLCC before any change in ownership, premises, or people with a financial interest takes effect
conditions.evidence_expected: Change requests filed with OLCC and OLCC approvals dated before each change took effect

conditions.title: Post the license at the premises where the public can see it
conditions.evidence_expected: A photo of the posted license at the Bailey Hill site

scan.confidence_notes: I am highly confident about everything read from the document: licensee, premises, tier, canopy, term, and the five conditions. The page is clear. I checked the rule (OAR 845-025-1190) that requires annual renewal. I did not confirm the exact 20-day cutoff in the current rule text, so the February 10, 2027 date comes from the license's own words, not from the rule. That date is my calculation. Two practical points I found but did not verify for this license: OLCC reportedly posts a renewal notice in its online licensing system about 90 days before expiration (around early December 2026), and producers may be asked for property owner consent at renewal. The signature line on the page is blank. That may just be how the copy was printed. If you need a signed original, ask OLCC. Ballot Measure 119's labor peace agreement requirement appears to apply to retailers, processors, and labs, not producers, but I am not certain of that.

OREGON LIQUOR AND CANNABIS COMMISSION
9079 SE McLoughlin Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97222
RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA PRODUCER LICENSE
License number: 020-1004763A8B2
Licensee: Evergreen Botanicals, LLC
Trade name: Evergreen Botanicals
Licensed premises: 2210 Bailey Hill Road, Eugene, Oregon 97405
License type: Producer — Tier II, Indoor
Canopy limit: 10,000 square feet mature plant canopy
Original issue date: March 3, 2022
Current term: March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027
Expiration date: March 2, 2027
This license is issued under ORS 475C and the rules of the Commission in OAR chapter 845, division 25, and
authorizes the licensee to produce marijuana at the licensed premises named above, subject to those rules and to the
conditions below.
Conditions of this license:
1. The license is valid only for the premises named above and is not transferable to any other location or person.
2. The license must be renewed annually. A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the
Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date. A licensee that has submitted a complete renewal
application before that date may continue to operate until the Commission acts on it.
3. All marijuana items at the premises must be tracked in the Cannabis Tracking System, and every employee who
handles marijuana items must hold a current marijuana worker permit issued by the Commission.
4. Video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 must be maintained at the premises and recordings kept for at
least 90 days.
5. Any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the persons with a financial interest in the licensee must be
reported to the Commission before it takes effect.
This license must be displayed at the licensed premises where it can be seen by the public.
Issued by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission
Date of issue for the current term: March 3, 2026
Authorized signature: ____________________ Licensing Director
